# Filter Magazine

> > Filter is an independent journalism outlet covering harm reduction, drug policy reform, and the lived experiences of people who use drugs.

Filter Magazine provides evidence-based reporting on drug policy, harm reduction strategies, criminal justice reform, and addiction recovery alternatives. The publication challenges stigmatizing narratives and advocates for public health approaches to substance use, featuring investigative journalism, personal narratives, and policy analysis from the United States and internationally.

## Key Topics

- harm reduction
- drug policy reform
- syringe exchange programs
- medication-assisted treatment (MAT)
- fentanyl exposure and testing
- cannabis legalization
- decriminalization
- 12-step alternatives
- vaping as harm reduction
- criminal justice reform
- public health approaches
- overdose prevention
- hepatitis A outbreaks
- drug misinformation
- stigma and media representation

## Harm Reduction & Public Health

- [What Happens When a Syringe Exchange Is Shut Down](https://filtermag.org/what-happens-when-a-syringe-exchange-is-shut-down): West Virginia HIV outbreak follows syringe exchange closure
- [New Study Shows Drug Users' Positive Responses to Learning They've Been Exposed to Fentanyl](https://filtermag.org/fentanyl-exposed-hair-test): Hair testing study shows fentanyl exposure awareness aids harm reduction
- [People Who Use Drugs Are Still Dying From Preventable Hepatitis A](https://filtermag.org/people-who-use-drugs-are-still-dying-from-preventable-hepatitis-a): CDC reports hepatitis A outbreaks in opioid-affected states
- [Vaping Isn't About Big Business—It's About Us, the Vapers](https://filtermag.org/vaping-isnt-about-big-business-its-about-us-the-vapers): Personal story of vaping as smoking cessation and harm reduction
- [FDA Cherry Picks Science in "Magic" Anti-Vaping Campaign](https://filtermag.org/fda-cherry-picks-science-in-magic-anti-vaping-campaign): FDA's The Real Cost campaign criticized for gateway theory claims

## Drug Policy & Criminal Justice Reform

- [Probation Officers Should Never Direct Medical Care for People With OUD](https://filtermag.org/probation-officers-should-never-direct-medical-care-for-people-with-oud): Oregon Senate Bill 910 limits probation officer control over MAT
- ["Now I Get to Have Good Problems"—Parole Preparation Project Works to Get More People Out Before It's Too Late](https://filtermag.org/now-i-get-to-have-good-problems-parole-preparation-project-works-to-get-more-people-out-before-its-too-late): Parole Preparation Project helps New York lifers secure release
- [Arrested While "Panicking on Meth"—An Hour Later, He Was Dead](https://filtermag.org/alex-billmeyer-dubuque-iowa-meth-death): Alex Billmeyer's death in Dubuque jail after meth-related arrest
- [Would You Pay More for Fair Trade Cocaine?](https://filtermag.org/would-you-pay-more-for-fair-trade-cocaine): Explores fair trade cocaine concept as drug regulation alternative

## Cannabis Legalization & Decriminalization

- [Berkeley, CA May Be Next City To Decriminalize Natural Psychedelics](https://filtermag.org/berkeley-decriminalize-psychedelics): Berkeley considers decriminalizing psilocybin and natural psychedelics
- [Equity and Expungement: Why Cannabis Activists Crashed SXSW](https://filtermag.org/equity-and-expungement-why-cannabis-activists-crashed-sxsw): Cannabis activists protest John Boehner at SXSW over hypocrisy
- [Poll: Cannabis Legalization Support Tracks the Paths of Gay and Interracial Marriage](https://filtermag.org/poll-cannabis-legalization-support-tracks-former-paths-of-gay-and-interracial-marriage): Gallup poll shows cannabis support mirrors marriage equality trends
- [DEA to Begin Reviewing Research-Cannabis Grow Applications "Soon"](https://filtermag.org/dea-cannabis-research): DEA faces court pressure over delayed cannabis research applications

- [Elton John and Bob Weir's Recovery Routes Are Closer Than They Seem](https://filtermag.org/elton-john-and-bob-weirs-recovery-routes-are-closer-than-they-seem): Compares Elton John and Grateful Dead's Bob Weir recovery journeys

- ["Zombies" and Rotting Flesh: The Media Just Loves Halloween-y Depictions of People Who Use Drugs](https://filtermag.org/flesh-rotting-zombies-back-from-the-dead-why-does-the-media-embrace-halloween-like-descriptions-of-people-who-use-drugs): Critiques dehumanizing zombie metaphors in drug use media coverage
- [Misinformation About So-Called "Terrorist Drug" Dispelled in New Report](https://filtermag.org/misinformation-about-so-called-terrorist-drug-dispelled-in-new-report): EMCDDA report debunks captagon misinformation in Middle East
